question.knowledge_point: Simplifying Expressions in Degrees Using the Sum and Difference Formulas
question.worked_solution:
Recall the difference formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(u-v)=\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v-\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the difference formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v={120}^{∘},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-{120}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡{120}^{∘}-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡{120}^{∘} \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot (-\frac{1}{2})-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot (\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}) \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}-\frac{\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2} \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

These simplifications hold on their original domains. q-1708 and q-65430 use the sine sum and difference formulas to obtain (sqrt(6)+sqrt(2))/4 and (sqrt(6)-sqrt(2))/4. The same formulas give q-141275=-(sin(x)+sqrt(3)cos(x))/2, q-65438=sqrt(2)(sin(x)-cos(x))/2, q-65437=sqrt(2)(sin(x)+cos(x))/2, and q-141284=-cos(x). q-109000 uses the quotient rule, giving v(t)=2t/(t²+1)². q-19299 differentiates to -4e^(-t)+6t-2, so v(2)=10-4e^(-2), rounded to 9.46. q-109012 has velocity -3/t², so speed at t=3 is 1/3 miles/h.
